name: ARTBITRAGE Trade
title: Trade — reference & computation for auction houses and galleries
essence: Artlogic manages; artbitrage speaks. No keys, no database, no funds, no take-rate.
provenance: Every number verified against primary sources (house Conditions of Business PDFs, legislation.gov.uk, gov.uk, ACE via UK Government Web Archive, ADAGP, Getty) by an 11-family verification pass on 2026-07-16; workflow wf_cd77c080-03f. Statuses: verified = primary source fetched and read; source-declared = stated by one primary-ish source; contested = sources conflict (both cited in notes).

coverage.included: Buyer's-premium schedules: Sotheby's (NY/London/HK/Paris), Christie's (7 salesrooms + wine), Bonhams (US/UK standard), Phillips (all salesrooms incl. watches/jewels/priority-bidding), China Guardian, Poly Auction. ARR UK+France. UK AML/VAT/export, EU AML/import. 7 material gates. 6 vocabularies.
known_gaps: Sotheby's Geneva/Singapore/UAE/Cologne/Milan bands exist on their help page but were not verified against individual CoB PDFs
Sotheby's Wine & Spirits schedule (flat 24% + 1% overhead premium) not yet encoded

disclosure.note: Reference arithmetic over cited public schedules. Confirm against the primary source before invoicing. Never legal, tax, or valuation advice.

arr.liable: Seller and the 'relevant person' are jointly and severally liable (reg 13(1)); relevant person = art market professional acting in priority order: seller's agent, else buyer's agent, else the buyer
arr.exemptions: Right does not apply where the seller acquired the work directly from the artist less than 3 years before the resale and the resale price is £10,000 or less (bought-as-stock exemption, reg 12; figure converted from EUR 10,000 to £10,000 on 2024-04-01)
arr.transitional: IMPORTANT: UK basis switched from EUR to GBP effective 2024-04-01 (SI 2023/1285), applying to contracts of sale dated on/after 2024-04-01. The *_eur field names below are legacy family-shape names; for the UK the values are GBP amounts. Pre-2024-04-01 contracts use the old EUR basis (threshold EUR 1,000, cap EUR 12,500, ECB conversion).

variances.note: Threshold EUR 750 excl. VAT (vs UK GBP 1,000); same 4/3/1/0.5/0.25% cumulative scale in EUR; cap EUR 12,500; ADAGP collects; extra exemption for first resale within 3 years of direct purchase from the artist at <= EUR 10,000

EU/EEA states remain on the EUR basis of Directive 2001/84/EC (default threshold up to EUR 3,000, most states set lower); the UK alone moved to a GBP basis on 2024-04-01, so cross-border UK/EU invoice math must not mix currencies

import_vat_art.mechanism: Qualifying works of art, antiques (100+ years old) and collectors' items are entered at a reduced import valuation: calculate the value for duty, add any additional costs, multiply the total by 25%, then apply the standard 20% VAT rate — 'By applying the 20% rate to the value it reduces the effective VAT rate to 5%' (gov.uk, How to value goods for import VAT)

thresholds.margin_scheme_note: Under the UK VAT margin scheme for second-hand goods, works of art, antiques and collectors' items, the seller accounts for VAT at 16.67% (one-sixth) of the difference between the purchase price and the selling price rather than on the full selling price.
thresholds.regulation: UK VAT valuation rules for imported works of art; VAT margin scheme
thresholds.notes: Mechanism and 5% effective rate quoted verbatim from the primary gov.uk valuation guidance (page last updated 1 Oct 2022); corroborated by HMRC internal manual IMPS05200 in search results. terms.meaning: Consignment agreement signed; property in the house's custody or pipeline
Lot description, estimate and images prepared; assigned to a sale
Presented at auction (live, online or timed)
Removed from sale before or during the auction
Hammer fell to a bid at or above the reserve
Failed to reach the reserve; returned to consignor or re-offered
Sold after the auction by private treaty at or around the reserve
Buyer paid in full and seller remitted; title passed

settlement-status.title: Settlement status

Outstanding as of measured_at — common enough in some markets to be a first-class state
House has exercised default remedies (cancellation, resale, interest)
Settlement state not disclosed by the source

meanings.christies: In Christie's opinion a work by the artist.
meanings.sothebys: The work is, in our best judgement, by the named artist.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion probably a work by the artist in whole or in part.
meanings.sothebys: In our opinion, probably a work by the artist but less certainty as to authorship is expressed than in the preceding category.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion a work executed in the studio or workshop of the artist, possibly under his supervision.
meanings.sothebys: In our opinion, a work by an unknown hand in the studio of the artist which may or may not have been executed under the artist's direction.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion a work of the period of the artist and showing his influence.
meanings.sothebys: In our opinion, a work by an as yet unidentified but distinct hand closely associated with the named artist but not necessarily his pupil.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion a work executed in the artist's style but not necessarily by a pupil.
In Christie's qualified opinion a work executed in the artist's style but of a later date.
meanings.sothebys: In our opinion, a work in the style of the artist and of a later date.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion a copy (of any date) of a work of the artist.
meanings.sothebys: In our opinion, a copy of a known work of the artist.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion the work has been signed/dated/inscribed by the artist.
meanings.sothebys: The term signed and/or dated and/or inscribed means that, in our opinion, a signature and/or date and/or inscription are from the hand of the artist.

meanings.christies: In Christie's qualified opinion the signature/date/inscription appears to be by a hand other than that of the artist.
meanings.sothebys: The term bears a signature and/or a date and/or an inscription means that, in our opinion, a signature and/or date and/or inscription have been added by another hand.
In our opinion, a work by a painter working in the artist's style, contemporary or nearly contemporary, but not necessarily his pupil.

catalogue-symbols.title: Catalogue symbols
catalogue-symbols.note: Symbols differ per house and per edition of the Conditions of Sale; each term carries its verification status.

terms.name: Minimum Price Guarantee
terms.meaning: Christie's has a direct financial interest in the lot: it has guaranteed the seller a minimum sale price for the work whatever the outcome of the sale.

terms.name: Third Party Guarantee / Irrevocable Bid
terms.meaning: Christie's has a direct financial interest in the lot and has funded all or part of that interest with the help of someone else: a third party has agreed prior to the auction to place an irrevocable written bid, taking on all or part of the risk of the lot not being sold; Christie's compensates the third party (fixed fee or amount calculated against final hammer price) provided the third party is not the successful bidder.

terms.name: Property owned by Christie's
terms.meaning: Owned by Christie's or another Christie's Group company in whole or part.

terms.name: Bidding by parties with an interest
terms.meaning: A party with a direct or indirect interest in the lot, who may have knowledge of the lot's reserve or other material information, may be bidding on the lot (e.g. beneficiary of an estate that consigned the lot, or a joint owner).

terms.name: No reserve
terms.meaning: Lot offered without reserve which will be sold to the highest bidder regardless of the pre-sale estimate in the catalogue.

terms.name: Artist's Resale Right
terms.meaning: Artist's resale right royalty applies to the lot; buyer pays an extra amount equal to the royalty (banded 4% / 3% / 1% / 0.5% / 0.25% of hammer-price portions, total capped at EUR 12,500 per lot). See Conditions of Sale section D3.

terms.name: Endangered species — export restrictions
terms.meaning: Lot incorporates material from endangered species which could result in export restrictions.

terms.name: Endangered species — display only
terms.meaning: Lot incorporates material from endangered species which is shown for display purposes only and is not for sale (e.g. alligator/crocodile watch straps, removed and retained by Christie's prior to shipment).

terms.name: US import restriction
terms.meaning: Lot which may not be able to be shipped to the US.

terms.name: Offsite storage
terms.meaning: Specified lots (sold and unsold) marked with a filled square that are not collected by the stated deadline will be removed to Christie's offsite storage — see the Storage and Collection page.

terms.name: VAT symbols (UK)
terms.meaning: VAT status of the lot: no symbol = UK Margin Scheme (VAT on buyer's premium, invoiced inclusively); † = standard UK VAT on hammer and buyer's premium; θ = zero-rated; * = imported under Temporary Admission, 5% import VAT on hammer; Ω = Temporary Admission with customs duty on hammer plus import VAT; α = treatment depends on whether buyer is EU/UK registered; ‡ = wine offered in bond.

terms.name: Watch batteries (dangerous goods)
terms.meaning: Lot incorporates batteries which may be designated 'dangerous goods' for air freight; batteries may be removed and retained prior to shipment outside the saleroom region (Hong Kong watches edition).

terms.name: No Reserve
terms.meaning: Unless indicated by a box, all lots in the catalogue are offered subject to a reserve; lots offered without reserve are designated by this symbol (reserve is the confidential minimum hammer price, generally a percentage of the low estimate and never above it).

terms.name: Guaranteed Property
terms.meaning: The seller of the lot has been guaranteed a minimum price from one auction or a series of auctions. The guarantee may be provided by Sotheby's or jointly by Sotheby's and a third party; Sotheby's and any third party providing the guarantee jointly benefit financially if the guaranteed lot sells successfully and may incur a loss if it does not — Sotheby's has a direct financial interest in the outcome.

terms.name: Irrevocable Bids
terms.meaning: A party has provided Sotheby's with an irrevocable bid on the lot that will be executed during the sale at a value that ensures the lot will sell. The irrevocable bidder, who may bid above the irrevocable bid, may be compensated (contingent fee, fixed fee or both); if the irrevocable bidder is the successful purchaser, compensation may be netted against the total purchase price. Irrevocable bidders advising others must disclose their financial interest.

terms.name: Interested Parties
terms.meaning: Parties with a direct or indirect interest in the lot may be bidding on it, including the beneficiary of an estate selling the lot or a joint owner; if such a party is the successful bidder they must pay the full buyer's premium and overhead premium, and interested parties may have knowledge of the reserve.

terms.name: Restricted Materials
terms.meaning: Lot identified at the time of cataloguing as containing organic material which may be subject to restrictions regarding import or export; absence of the symbol is not a warranty that there are no restrictions.

terms.name: Monumental
terms.meaning: Lot may, in Sotheby's opinion, require special handling or shipping services due to size or other physical considerations.

terms.name: Premium Lot
terms.meaning: To bid, a Premium Lot pre-registration application must be completed at least three working days before the sale (symbol shown as ◇ on the lot's webpage); Sotheby's decision whether to accept the application is final.

terms.name: US Import Tariff
terms.meaning: Lot subject to a US import tariff — a percentage of the value declared upon entry into the United States, not based on the final hammer price — included in the purchase price.

terms.name: Property Subject to the Artist's Resale Right
terms.meaning: Purchase of the lot is subject to payment of the Artist's Resale Right royalty, calculated as a banded percentage of the hammer price with a maximum of EUR/GBP 12,500 per work.

terms.name: National Patrimony / National Heritage lot
terms.meaning: Lot is part of a national heritage regime (Buying at Auction guide: part of the National Heritage of Mexico, cannot be permanently exported from Mexico; offered for sale in New York but not available in New York for inspection or delivery — buyer takes delivery in Mexico).

terms.name: Financing Eligible
terms.meaning: Financing of up to 50% of the lot's low auction estimate is available for eligible borrowers through Sotheby's Financial Services.
